questions.q: In traditional Maranao architecture, what is the term for the carved, wing-like house beams that protrude in front of the Torogan, typically shaped like a prow of a boat and adorned with intricate okir carvings?
questions.n: The panolong is the iconic flaring beam ornament displaying boat-prow geometry and detailed serpent or floral okir motifs.

questions.q: The Torogan is famously built to withstand earthquakes. What is the name of the massive, central wooden pillars or posts that support the entire structure, which are traditionally placed on top of large stones rather than buried in the ground to allow the house to sway safely?
questions.n: The tukud are the massive foundation columns sitting directly on stone boulders to absorb seismic energy through sliding friction.

questions.q: When looking at the very top of a Torogan house, you will see a crown-like finial or apex ornament sitting on the roof ridge, which symbolizes high social status and royalty. What is this pinnacle called?
questions.n: The diongal serves as the royal apex finial directly adorning the roof ridge line of the sultan's house.

questions.q: One of the most prominent design motifs found in Maranao woodcarving represents a stylized, growing fern leaf, symbolizing life, continuity, and prosperity. What is this specific architectural ornament called?
questions.n: Pako Rabong translates to an organic, unfolding fern shoot motif that dominates organic okir relief carving.

questions.q: To ensure privacy and division within the otherwise wide, wall-less interior of the Torogan, what is the term for the woven fabric or wooden screen partitions used to separate the sultan's family quarters from the rest of the clan?
questions.n: Tapuwilih refers to the temporary, adjustable fabric hangings or screen partitions that demarcate spaces within the communal hall.

questions.q: The Torogan serves as a royal residence and a communal space. What is the term for the elevated, decorated wooden bed or royal sleeping platform reserved exclusively for the Sultan or the highest-ranking member of the household?
questions.n: The panggao is the highly ornamental, raised state bed frame reserved for royalty within the communal layout.

questions.q: Walkways and structural edges of the Torogan often feature decorative, jagged, or scalloped wooden borders that mimic the appearance of a slice of starfruit. What is this specific fringe ornament called?
questions.n: Barimbingan refers specifically to the stylized, segmented wood profiles inspired by the starfruit edge design.

questions.q: The interior of a Torogan is a massive, open hall without permanent rooms. What is the Maranao term for the main flooring, traditionally made of thick hardwood planks or split bamboo, where community gatherings, weddings, and judicial trials take place?
questions.n: Lantay is the common architectural term for the functional hardwood or bamboo flooring deck in Maranao structures.

questions.q: In the traditional Ifugao Fale, what is the term for the large, cylindrical wooden discs fitted around the four main house posts to prevent rodents from climbing up into the living quarters and granary?
questions.n: The halipan functions explicitly as a mechanical rat guard barrier installed along the smooth post shaft.

questions.q: The interior of the Fale features a functional three-level system. What is the specific native term used for the third-level attic or loft space situated directly beneath the steep, pyramidal roof, which primarily serves as a storage area for unhusked rice grains?
questions.n: The pala functions as the elevated granary loft space protected by the high heat and smoke rising from the fireplace below.

questions.q: The Fale is celebrated as a masterclass in joinery, constructed entirely without nails. What is the name of the four secondary vertical wooden posts (or upper columns) on the main living level that are mortised into the outer floor beams and enclosed by a girt at the top to form the structural 'house cage'?
questions.n: Bagat are the four inner wall posts that interlock into the floor joist beams to carry the wallboards and roof framing.

questions.q: Serving as a crucial horizontal stabilizer for the wall system, what is the term for the chest-level transverse wooden beam into which the vertical wallboards are neatly rabbeted or slotted?
questions.n: The huklub is the perimeter wall girt or horizontal tie beam that secures the wallboards structurally around the living box.

questions.q: To insulate the dark, windowless interior from the elements, the walls slant outward to the waistline. What is the Ifugao term for these thick, heavy wooden wallboards that enclose the four sides of the one-room living quarters?
questions.n: Ga-ob is the specific vernacular term for the thick timber cladding planks that build up the slanted exterior walls.

questions.q: An essential piece of interior utility, the Fale features a built-in wooden shelf system that stretches outwards from the wall headers to the underside of the roof framework. What is this structural storage shelf called?
questions.n: The patuat is an interior horizontal shelf assembly supported by the roof rafters to maximize overhead storage utility.

questions.q: Within the pundapalan (earthen fireplace area), drying wood and preserving meat is highly prioritized. What is the term for the wide, slatted wooden shelf or open rack suspended directly above the hearth used to dry wet firewood and smoke food items?
questions.n: The fu-ig is the dedicated wood/food drying shelf frame suspended immediately above the open fireplace flames.

questions.q: The entire weight of the timber framing rests upon a robust horizontal foundation network. What is the specific regional term for the secondary floor joists or ties that run across the main girders to hold up the heavy hardwood floorboards (dotal)?
questions.n: Gatis are the floor joists placed perpendicular to the major log girders to safely distribute the interior floor loads.

questions.q: In the vernacular architecture of Batanes, the Rakuh is built with immense structural mass to resist seismic and typhoon forces. What is the material or element used for the thick, heavy masonry walls made of fieldstones or corals bound tightly together by a traditional lime and mud mortar?
questions.n: Sapa refers directly to the thick, massive limestone and coral mortar wall assembly characteristic of Ivatan storm-shelter houses.

questions.q: Batanes is frequently hit by powerful typhoons with destructive winds. To keep the thick, multi-layered cogon grass roof from being blown away, what is the term for the large protective roof net made of strong, braided ropes thrown completely over the thatch and tied securely to ground pegs or built-in wall anchors?
questions.n: The panpet is the specialized heavy-duty rope storm net overlaid across the cogon thatch surface to hold it down against high winds.

questions.q: The Rakuh features a highly specialized multi-layered roof framework to manage the extreme tropical weather. What is the specific Ivatan term for the lower roof ridge cover that is tightly compressed by the top layer of yayis (battens) to establish a watertight seal at the apex?
questions.n: The vuvong is the specialized ridge cap layer of cogon that seals the crown apex of the roof structure from leakage.

questions.q: To preserve structural stability during earthquakes, the Rakuh functions through a smart 'house-within-a-house' system where the roof weight is carried by internal wooden posts rather than the exterior masonry. What is the structural term for the main interior volume, enclosed attic space, or upper floor cavity directly underneath the heavy thatched roof?
questions.n: The kuvub represents the high attic inner void space protected by the framing network underneath the deep cogon grass profiles.

questions.q: While the traditional Ivatan residence is structurally split into distinct living zones, what is the specific name or term used for the main, two-story stone house structure that houses the primary living and sleeping quarters for the Ivatan family?
questions.n: The rakuh is specifically the large, thick-walled masonry structural unit serving as the main domestic center.

questions.q: Due to the extreme winds, the openings of an Ivatan house are placed strategically, leaving one blank wall facing the direction of the strongest seasonal typhoons. What is the term for the windowed or open porch-like side of the house that serves as a space for ventilation, viewing, and lounging?
questions.n: The pahayahan is the open, well-ventilated window or porch section of the house layout oriented away from harsh prevailing storms.

questions.q: To prevent accidental structural fires from spreading to the main living quarters and to manage smoke from cooking, the Ivatan residential compound splits its functions. What is the separate, detached structure or auxiliary room used exclusively as the cooking area and hearth?
questions.n: The kusina (or auxiliary cooking house) is built separate from the main living volume to safeguard the main cogon roof from cooking sparks.

questions.q: While the external shell of the Rakuh relies on brutal stone masonry, the interior flooring requires a clean, level surface for sleeping and daily activities. What is the vernacular term for the main internal timber floor planks or structural deck boarding used inside the living quarters?
questions.n: Lantay is the common architectural term used across multiple Philippine vernacular designs to describe interior wood floorboards.
